fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Queued/turning/parking vehicle interference within the functional area of a new closely-spaced service road junction on a corridor with recorded accident issues is a core, substantive preliminary-design-stage safety concern.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal interference claim is backed by verbatim quoted text under EV-US-016 matching the finding statement, exceeding registry-id-only citation; no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as an FHWA-style safety_concern with null normative basis rather than a compliance assertion, keeping safety and compliance categorically distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommends concrete, viable treatments (turn restrictions plus relocating specified stalls outside the intersection functional area) that directly address the identified conflict mechanism.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrian and cyclist presence along the commercial corridor is explicitly acknowledged even though the conflict mechanism itself is vehicle-to-vehicle, matching the acknowledge-but-not-applicable tier.

justifications.substance: Closely spaced signal coordination and queue storage on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a core, substantive preliminary-design-stage safety issue with a real crash mechanism (spillback blocking the upstream intersection).
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim of ~650 ft signal spacing is supported by the verbatim quote in EV-US-001, and the queue-spillback mechanism is transparently labeled as a derived inference rather than invented fact.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern/check under FHWA RSA semantics, keeping the safety issue categorically distinct from any compliance assertion.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable for preliminary design (coordinate adjacent signals, install Do Not Block Intersection signs, upgrade signing/display conspicuity) and is a viable, standard mitigation package.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged with reasoned scoping to vehicle occupants, but no VRU-specific impact analysis is provided, matching the 'not applicable but acknowledged' tier.
